entries.title: Juvenile Justice Center New Courtroom Design
entries.description: The County's historical design account describes a $1.2 million renovation to create a 3,276-square-foot courtroom for the Second Judicial District Court within the existing John Brown Juvenile Justice Center. It reports completed design by Studio Southwest Architects and an anticipated early-2020 construction start.
entries.public_value_finding: The two short official accounts are meaningful together as an explicitly historical facility-investment group. Each contributes a distinct project scope and budget while the shared introduction supplies location, relationship and timing limitations. Separate links preserve the reader ability to inspect each County source without manufacturing an archival master or implying completed work.

entries.title: Bernalillo County Youth Services Center Project

It identifies Vigil & Associates Architects and an anticipated early-2020 construction start.

section_heading: Historical County Youth Justice Facility Projects
group_introduction: These two official County project accounts describe different renovations at 5100 Second Street NW in Albuquerque: building and safety improvements at the Youth Services Center, and a courtroom within the John Brown Juvenile Justice Center. Both retain anticipated early-2020 construction schedules; they document historical design scopes and budgets, rather than establish current project status or completed work.
cross_listing: None: these sources document facility infrastructure and capital costs, not justice outcome datasets, and lack substantive transportation content.
standalone_entry_review: Individual short summaries lack the contextual relationship and timing qualifications supplied by this curated two-component group. Both official links remain individually accessible.
archive_requirements: Maintained official HTML pages have no selected static original; no R2 master, screenshot archive link, object upload, or archival claim. The tracked evidence bundle is solely a research witness.
